title: Emprendimiento académico y uso de dispositivos electrónicos programables como estrategia de innovación pedagógica
abstract: La presente investigación analiza la convergencia entre el emprendimiento académico y el uso de dispositivos electrónicos programables como una estrategia de innovación pedagógica en el entorno educativo contemporáneo. A través de una revisión documental sistemática de la literatura científica de los últimos cinco años indexada en bases regionales e internacionales de alto impacto, se evalúa cómo la computación física, el movimiento hacedor (maker) y la robótica educativa reconfiguran el proceso de enseñanza-aprendizaje. Los resultados evidencian que el diseño y la programación de hardware libre (particularmente la plataforma Arduino) potencian no solo destrezas técnicas en disciplinas STEAM, sino también habilidades transversales indispensables para el desarrollo de una mentalidad emprendedora, tales como la resiliencia ante el error, la autoeficacia y la resolución de problemas complejos. No obstante, la discusión revela importantes tensiones entre las aspiraciones didácticas de estas herramientas tecnológicas y las barreras de capacitación docente y de infraestructura sistémica que persisten en la región latinoamericana. Se concluye que, para garantizar el éxito de estas estrategias de innovación pedagógica, es imperativo establecer políticas de formación docente continua y consolidar ecosistemas universitarios que mitiguen las trabas burocráticas y financieras, facilitando la conversión de proyectos de aula en emprendimientos tecnológicos viables y sostenibles.

title: A Study of Belief Revision Postulates in Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: We investigate the belief revision problem in epistemic planning, i.e., what will be the beliefs of all agents in a multi-agent system after an agent gains the belief in some state property. Based on the standard representation in epistemic planning of agents' beliefs via a single multi-agent Kripke model, we generalize the classical AGM belief revision postulates to the multi-agent setting, with the aim to provide a formal framework for evaluating dynamic epistemic reasoning frameworks in which the beliefs of all agents as the result of actions are computed. As an example of a simple operator that satisfies all of the generalized AGM postulates, we present generalized full-meet multi-agent belief revision. We moreover define a generalization of the standard postulates for iterated revision, present a more sophisticated, event model based revision operator, and discuss the potential issues in defining an epistemic operator on Kripke models that can satisfy all of the generalized postulates for iterated multi-agent belief revision.

title: AI in Climate Research
abstract: As global environmental challenges intensify, the need for innovative, sustainable solutions has become urgent. Artificial intelligence (AI) is emerging as a powerful tool in addressing these issues, with the potential to transform how we monitor, manage, and mitigate environmental impacts. This research explores the role of AI in environmental science, focusing on its applications in areas such as climate modeling, biodiversity conservation, and resource management. By reviewing existing literature and case studies, the study demonstrates that AI significantly improves the precision of environmental monitoring, enables advanced predictive analytics, and supports informed decision-making—key factors for achieving sustainable development. However, the research also identifies critical challenges that hinder the full potential of AI, including issues with data quality, the complexity of ethical considerations, and the need for stronger interdisciplinary collaboration. Despite these hurdles, AI offers substantial opportunities to drive environmental innovation and shape future environmental policies. In addition to highlighting AI’s transformative capabilities, the research also delves into the challenges that must be overcome to unlock its full potential. These include issues related to data quality, accessibility, and interoperability, as well as the complexity of ethical considerations such as privacy, fairness, and accountability in the use of AI for environmental purposes. The chapter concludes by outlining strategic recommendations for research and policy development, aimed at maximizing the benefits of AI in addressing pressing ecological concerns on a global scale.

title: Flexible Error Modeling and Analysis of SiPho JTC Accelerators for CNNs
abstract: This paper describes a system for modeling nonidealities in a silicon-photonic joint transform correlator (JTC) used as an accelerator for convolutional neural networks (CNNs). The system is used to determine which nonidealities have the greatest impact on end-to-end model accuracy, which helps determine what design choices can be made at the block and system level to improve performance. We create a digital twin of the on-chip 1D JTC using transfer functions fitted from simulations, then introduce a scalar α that mixes ideal and realized behaviors. We quantify the α -dependent model accuracy on CIFAR-10 and SNDR differences at both the joint-power spectrum (JPS) and the JTC output. The framework allows quantification of block- and system-level sensitivities, informing design choices by isolating the accuracy bottlenecks within the system.

title: Optimizing neural networks via Hilfer–Katugampola fractional derivatives: A theoretical and experimental study
abstract: This paper proposes a novel hybrid optimization approach designed to improve convergence efficiency and model performance in classification tasks. For the purpose of improving stability and ensuring fast learning in the training process, complementary optimization approaches have been adopted. Benchmarked datasets are used in this research for conducting experiments; the findings of which will be compared with those of commonly used optimizers. It was found out that the proposed method ensures computational efficiency and fast convergence, as well as reduced training loss and classification accuracy.

title: Revisiting training-free tabular models: A robustness and efficiency study
abstract: Training-free classifiers for tabular data eliminate dataset-specific model fitting by pre-training a meta-learner that generalises to new tasks without gradient updates. HyperFast Bonet et al. (2024), introduced at AAAI 2024, generates task-specific classifier weights through a hypernetwork and is promoted as suitable for resource-constrained deployment. However, prior evaluations focus primarily on clean benchmark datasets and do not assess common real-world challenges such as noise, missing values, and limited labelled data. We conduct a systematic evaluation across 17 binary classification datasets from UCI, OpenML, and Kaggle, covering domains including fraud detection, predictive maintenance, and healthcare. Six models are compared: HyperFast (default and tuned), Logistic Regression, LightGBM, XGBoost, and Random Forest. Experiments span 15 random seeds and 13 conditions per dataset, yielding 19,890 model evaluations. HyperFast (default) wins none of the 224 evaluated conditions and is significantly worse than the best-performing model in 206 cases. HyperFast-Tuned wins 30 conditions, primarily on highly imbalanced datasets under degraded data conditions, but requires between 81 and 16,191 times more inference time than Logistic Regression. Logistic Regression achieves 86 condition wins and LightGBM 61, together accounting for 66 Our findings indicate that training-free inference does not eliminate computational cost but shifts it from offline training to deployment-time inference. Across the evaluated datasets and robustness conditions, classical and gradient-boosted methods generally provide superior accuracy-runtime trade-offs, while HyperFast-Tuned offers advantages only in a limited set of challenging scenarios.

title: Hierarchical identity-based encryption with receiver selective opening security in the multi-challenge setting
abstract: Receiver selective opening (RSO) security considers the security of encryption schemes under the scenario of a single sender and multiple receivers, where an adversary is allowed to adaptively corrupt some receivers’ secret keys. RSO security has been proven to be more secure than indistinguishability-based security notions. A lot of research has focused on RSO security in terms of public-key encryption and identity-based encryption (IBE); however, hierarchical IBE (HIBE), which is a generalization of IBE, is still lacking in the study, and how to obtain such a construction remains an open problem. To address this gap, we initiate a study of RSO security on HIBE in this work. Precisely, we first formalize the definition of simulation-based RSO against identity-chosen-plaintext/ciphertext attacks in the k-challenge setting (SIM-ID-RSO $$_k$$ -CPA/CCA) for HIBE. We then present generic SIM-ID-RSO $$_k$$ -CCA secure HIBE constructions by introducing the double secret key paradigm. Specifically, we show that a SIM-ID-RSO $$_k$$ -CCA secure HIBE scheme can be obtained from an IND-ID-CPA secure HIBE scheme as well as a one-time signature scheme that satisfies strong unforgeability. Through our general construction, we can derive various concrete schemes based on different hard assumptions (e.g., lattice-based and pairing-based SIM-ID-RSO $$_k$$ -CCA secure HIBE schemes) according to usage requirements.

title: STN-TGAT: Top-K Portfolio Construction via Prior-Guided Graph Attention with Learnable Soft-Threshold Sparsification
abstract: This paper tackles the problem of stock ranking and portfolio construction under realistic investment settings by jointly modeling temporal dynamics and cross-sectional dependencies. We propose the Soft-Threshold NMI-prior Transformer Graph Attention Network (STN-TGAT), which integrates a temporal Transformer with a Graph Attention Network to capture long-horizon sequential patterns and dynamic inter-stock relationships. An NMI-based prior graph combined with a soft-threshold sparsification mechanism enhances structural robustness by mitigating noisy correlations while preserving informative connections. The portfolio formation process incorporates practical considerations, including Top-5 selection within the Top-50 $S\&P$ 500 constituents, explicit weight allocation, and transaction cost adjustment, thereby aligning the evaluation with real-world trading conditions. Empirical results on real-world data demonstrate that STN-TGAT consistently outperforms benchmark models from predictive accuracy and investment profitability measured by portfolio returns. These findings suggest that combining decision-aligned training with adaptive relational modeling provides a coherent and practically effective framework for data-driven portfolio construction.

title: Reliability-Aware CT-MRI Registration: A Quality Engineering Framework with Stability Analysis and Risk Classification
abstract: Multimodal CT-MRI registration is central to image-guided radiotherapy, surgical navigation, and diagnostic workflows, but most pipelines report only aggregate quality metrics without per-case reliability signals. We propose a reliability-aware framework that converts registration quality into Green/Yellow/Red risk categories using data-learned thresholds. CT images were registered to T1-weighted MRI using rigid and affine transformations on 90 paired slices from 18 patients across brain, abdominal, and neck anatomies. Reliability was assessed using Delta NMI, Delta SSIM, Dice overlap, registration stability, and inverse consistency error, combined into a single score R. Thresholds learned from training patients were applied unchanged to held-out test patients. Affine registration outperformed rigid registration on NMI and SSIM, yielding 44% Green classifications versus 33% for rigid. Reliability-filtered registrations improved the average alignment profile compared with unfiltered methods. Per-anatomy analysis showed substantial variation, with stronger reliability for abdominal registrations than brain registrations. Weight sensitivity analysis identified Dice overlap as the dominant reliability component. The proposed framework provides an interpretable quality-control layer for multimodal registration, while risk thresholds reflect statistical rather than clinical validation.

title: GAIA: Geometry-Adaptive Operator Learning for Forward and Inverse Problems
abstract: Operator learning for partial differential equations (PDEs) on arbitrary geometries builds fast neural surrogates for large-scale simulation. Although recent geometry-adaptive neural operators have made substantial progress, they are mainly designed for forward problems in which inputs and outputs share the same spatial domain. This limits their applicability for boundary value problems (BVPs) and inverse problems, where inputs and outputs may live on different domains. We introduce the Geometry-Adaptive Integral Autoencoder (GAIA), an operator learning model that encodes the domain boundary and the interior field distribution into geometry tokens, and conditions integral transform layers on these tokens via cross-attention, allowing the kernel to adapt locally to geometric features. This yields a single architecture for forward (including BVPs) and inverse problems on arbitrary domains in one pass, without retraining, iterative optimization, or graph construction. We evaluate GAIA on seven 2D and 3D benchmarks, four of which are new or substantially extended benchmarks for inverse problems and BVP: electrical impedance tomography, optical tomography, 3D Darcy flow on varying geometries, and a modified setting of Poisson BVP on mechanical components benchmark (MCB). GAIA sets new state-of-the-art results on every inverse and BVP task, reducing median relative $L^2$ error by 64% on airfoil flow reconstruction and 27% on EIT relative to the next best amortized method, and outperforming all baselines on every shape category of MCB. On other forward problems, GAIA is competitive with specialized solvers while maintaining stable accuracy across point resolutions on which transformer-based baselines degrade.

title: Not All Prediction Targets Keep Training-Free Diffusion Guidance on the Manifold
abstract: Training-free guidance (TFG) steers a pretrained diffusion model toward a desired attribute at inference. To be effective, this guidance must be applied from the earliest, high-noise steps of sampling. Because its objective (a classifier or energy) is defined on clean images, $ε$- and $v$-prediction models must first estimate the clean image $\hat{x}$ from the noisy state at each step, and the accuracy of that estimate determines how easily guidance drifts off the data manifold. $x$-prediction, a recent alternative, outputs the clean image directly, removing this source of error even at high noise. This is our motivation. We provide a theoretical analysis of how each prediction target shapes this accuracy, and introduce guided-class FID (Child FID), a metric that exposes the manifold damage standard evaluation misses. Experiments on a new fine-grained bird benchmark and on style transfer confirm that $x$-prediction keeps guided samples on the manifold most reliably, making it the strongest foundation for training-free guidance. evidence.title: Not All Prediction Targets Keep Training-Free Diffusion Guidance on the Manifold
evidence.abstract: Training-free guidance (TFG) steers a pretrained diffusion model toward a desired attribute at inference. To be effective, this guidance must be applied from the earliest, high-noise steps of sampling. Because its objective (a classifier or energy) is defined on clean images, $ε$- and $v$-prediction models must first estimate the clean image $\hat{x}$ from the noisy state at each step, and the accuracy of that estimate determines how easily guidance drifts off the data manifold. $x$-prediction, a recent alternative, outputs the clean image directly, removing this source of error even at high noise. This is our motivation. We provide a theoretical analysis of how each prediction target shapes this accuracy, and introduce guided-class FID (Child FID), a metric that exposes the manifold damage standard evaluation misses. Experiments on a new fine-grained bird benchmark and on style transfer confirm that $x$-prediction keeps guided samples on the manifold most reliably, making it the strongest foundation for training-free guidance. Code is available at https://github.com/ManLuML/on-manifold-tfg

title: A Model Context Protocol Framework for Bridge Data Generation with Large Language Model Integration
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong capabilities in natural language understanding and reasoning, however, integrating them with domain-specific engineering tools remains a persistent challenge. This paper introduces BrDSL-MCP, a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server designed to connect conversational AI interfaces with structural engineering workflows for bridge specification data generation. The proposed system supports real-time interaction between LLMs and bridge engineering tools, enabling parametric design generation, finite element analysis (FEA) via Abaqus, within a unified, natural-language-driven loop. We detail the architectural choices that facilitate reliable tool composition and demonstrate how the system supports bridge data generation through conversational interaction. Case studies indicate that engineers can complete design iterations faster than with conventional manual workflows, while retaining full authority over final engineering decisions.

title: User Preference Model-Based Sentiment-Semantic Corresponding Method for Korean Text Translation
abstract: In order to solve the problems of poor matching accuracy and long time-consuming in traditional Korean text translation emotional semantic matching methods, this paper proposes research on a Korean text translation emotional semantic matching method considering a user preference model. Build a user preference model, input that obtained emotional space position perception vector into the user preference model, correcting the translation semantic result according to the user’s emotional preference, determining the freshness of keyword features, calculating the freshness weight, generating user preferences, and calculating the similarity of interest vectors among users, on this basis, obtaining a Korean text data set, and using Word2Vec model to map individual words in natural language corpus to vectors to extract Korean text translation features; By inputting word vectors into DPCNN, depth features are extracted to classify text emotions. The semantic matching model of translated text is constructed by sentence representation, and the emotional space position perception vector is introduced to deeply match the emotional semantics of Korean translated text, which makes the semantic matching result more accurate. The experimental results show that the semantic matching accuracy of Korean translation text under this method is 99.6%, and the matching time is 3.6s, which can effectively improve the accuracy of emotional semantic matching and further improve the translation effect of Korean text.

title: Understanding Privacy and Quality Tradeoffs in Synthetic Network Data
abstract: The limited availability of high-quality computer networking data, and the privacy risks of sharing what does exist, has prompted development of ML-based methods for generating synthetic network data that mimics real communication between networked devices. The viability of these models hinges on both the quality of their output and how well they preserve private information encoded in their training data. Prior work has sought to address this by training models with differential privacy (DP). However, how this choice affects the actual privacy of the training data, and subsequently the quality of the generated output, is not well understood. In this work, we analyze the relationship between privacy and quality in generative network data models. Using the success of membership inference attacks (MIAs) as the metric for privacy, we observe that whether DP mitigates MIAs depends heavily on model architecture and representation of network data used for training. In particular, we empirically find that some approaches to generating synthetic network data train models that heavily skew towards either overgeneralizing or undergeneralizing to their training data, resulting in poor or inconsistent MIA performance. In these cases, using DP does not yield substantive improvements in vulnerability to MIAs. As for the quality of generated data, we find that DP synthetic network data can retain statistical similarity to real data even under strict privacy budgets, and that downstream models (e.g., classifiers, regressors) trained on this data tend to achieve at least as good accuracy as models trained on non-DP data. These results suggest that DP, depending on the model, offers protection against MIAs without degrading the utility of the generated output, and in some cases, improves utility.

title: Artificial Intelligence Leaders: Literature Review and Future Direction
abstract: From simple text input and calculations to analyzing and interpreting complex data, the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in organizational management has gradually evolved from an auxiliary tool to an intelligent agent with leadership functions. By systematically reviewing 51 relevant literatures, this paper summarizes AI’s significant advantages in information processing, decision-making efficiency, procedure execution, and conflict mediation, while pointing out its shortcomings in emotional resonance, value judgment, and creative tasks. It analyzes the diverse power forms of AI leaders, including legitimate power, reward power, coercive power, expert power, referent power, and biopower, and further sorts out the dual impacts that AI may bring as a leader. Finally, this paper proposes that future research should focus on exploring the emergence mechanism, subsequent effects, and ethical issues of AI leadership, and attempt to construct a future-oriented human-machine leadership mechanism, so as to deepen the theoretical understanding of AI’s leadership role in organizations and provide guidance and reference for enterprises to rationally deploy AI leaders.

title: A Universal Structural Framework for Intelligence
abstract: This paper proposes a structural-functional framework for defining intelligence at a macro level. Rather than viewing intelligence as a measure of performance, task success, or domain-specific capability, the framework characterises it as a property that emerges from the interaction among information, structure, weighting, and constraint. The central claim is that intelligence is not determined solely by the quantity of information within a system, but by the system's capacity to traverse meaningful pathways through a structured, weighted informational space. The framework is represented by I = C × Φ(S, St, W), where intelligence emerges from the constrained space of traversable inference paths generated within a structured information system. The model is intended as a general framework applicable to biological, artificial, computational, and hypothetical systems. The paper discusses the core definition, structural representation, conceptual advantages, and outlines key open problems, including the formal definition of Φ and its subproblems related to information (S), structure (St), weights (W), constraints (C), and temporal evolution.The framework is also available at: https://github.com/elvisho754-svg/Universal-intelligence-framework

title: Multimodal Knowledge Graph Completion Model with Cross-Modal Dual-Interaction and Semantic Reasoning
authors: GUO Wei, ZHAO Tongming, QU Haicheng
abstract: Multimodal knowledge graph completion aims to solve the problem of missing entities and relationships in the graph, but its performance is often limited by the challenges of insufficient inter-modal interactions and semantic spurious associations. Existing approaches focus on modal fusion and model generation, but neglect the mining of deep cross-modal semantic associations and the destruction of reasoning logic by false causal chains. To address the above problems, this paper proposes the OXHS (orthogonal-X-hierarchical-causal) model, which achieves efficient complementation of multimodal knowledge graphs through the modal dual-interaction mechanism and cross-modal semantic reasoning module. The modal dual-interaction module combines self-attention and cross-modal cross-attention to hierarchically mine intra-modal contextual features and inter-modal non-linear associations. The cross-modal semantic inference module contains a three-order design. Firstly, an orthogonal contrast causal decoupler is proposed to decouple causal semantics and noise through dynamic gating and contrast learning to suppress the influence of false associations on inference. Secondly, a knowledge enhancement module is utilized to realize the alignment of causal semantics and graph structure. Finally, an uncertainty-aware fusion strategy is introduced to dynamically balance the contribution of causality and noise to improve inference robustness. Experiments on three benchmark datasets show that OXHS significantly outperforms the benchmark methods in the link prediction task in terms of Hits@1 metric, with an average improvement of 4.62 percentage points compared with the suboptimal benchmark, demonstrating excellent accurate reasoning capability.

title: New paradigm of forestry and grassland research driven by artificial intelligence
abstract: Addressing the current limitations in forestry and grassland research, particularly in cross-scale system cognition, complex process mechanism representation, and multi-scenario simulation, this study proposes an artificial intelligence-driven paradigm reconstruction framework, to shift the research model from experience-oriented approaches toward data- and intelligence-driven integration. On this basis, the study systematically establishes a multidimensional mapping between artificial intelligence and forestry and grassland research across research objects, processes, and objectives, and clarifies their intrinsic coupling mechanisms and technical pathways. Furthermore, it develops a foundational capability system to support the new paradigm from four key dimensions: data, computing power, models, and applications. By examining typical application scenarios—including ecological governance, resource management, forest cultivation, and industrial development—the study further explores the practical modes and application potential of artificial intelligence in forestry and grassland science. This work is expected to provide a useful reference for promoting the intelligent and systematic transformation of forestry and grassland research in China.

title: ALM–ASP: A Functional Agentic Architecture for Answer Set Programming
abstract: Answer Set Programming (ASP) is a declarative formalism widely used in knowledge representation and reasoning for modeling and solving combinatorial problems, yet current Large Language Models (LLMs) often struggle to generate correct programs from natural language specifications. This difficulty stems both from the limited presence of ASP in training corpora and from the strict syntactic and semantic constraints imposed by stable model semantics. We introduce ALM–ASP (Agentic Loop for Modeling in ASP), a multi-agent architecture for automatic ASP modeling grounded in a functional model of language agents equipped with tools and persistent state. ALM–ASP instantiates this model via two interacting agents: a Modeler, which incrementally constructs candidate ASP programs, and a Validator, which assesses their alignment with the original specification and provides feedback for refinement. The agents interact through a shared ASP execution environment backed by the CLINGO engine, yielding an iterative construct–validate loop. An empirical evaluation on a challenging subset of CP–Bench and on problems from recent LP/CP Programming Contests shows that ALM–ASP significantly improves both syntactic validity and end-to-end correctness over general-purpose LLM baselines, and also achieves improved instance coverage compared to the closest agentic alternative, CP–Agent.

title: CBOR Object Signing and Encryption (COSE) Hash Envelope
abstract: This document defines new CBOR Object Signing and Encryption (COSE) header parameters for signaling a payload as an output of a hash function. This mechanism enables faster validation, as access to the original payload is not required for signature validation. Additionally, hints of the hashed payload's content format and availability are defined, providing references to optional discovery mechanisms that can help to find the original payload content.

title: Drivers and barriers of learning MBSE: design and validation of a RAG-based AI chatbot leveraging smart views
abstract: Learning MBSE is hindered by abstraction and complex tools. This paper identifies barriers via literature review and interviews to design a RAG-based chatbot acting as a “smart view” for contextual guidance. Evaluated through a semester-long field study and a controlled experiment, the prototype shows high usability and reduces cognitive load. While performance is comparable to traditional e-books, the RAG-enabled system effectively mitigates entry-level barriers and aids authentic project work through stepwise tutoring, offering a scalable, interactive complement to MBSE education.

title: The nuclear route: sharp asymptotics of ERM in overparameterized quadratic networks *
abstract: Abstract We study the high-dimensional asymptotics of empirical risk minimization (ERM) in over-parametrized two-layer neural networks with quadratic activations trained on synthetic data. We derive sharp asymptotics for both training and test errors by mapping the ℓ 2 -regularized learning problem to a convex matrix sensing task with nuclear norm penalization. This reveals that capacity control in such networks emerges from a low-rank structure in the learned feature maps. Our results characterize the global minima of the loss and yield precise generalization thresholds, showing how the width of the target function governs learnability. This analysis bridges and extends ideas from spin-glass methods, matrix factorization, and convex optimization and emphasizes the deep link between low-rank matrix sensing and learning in quadratic neural networks.

title: Chaotic-based BVM algorithm for solving optimization and engineering problems
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Chaotic-Based BVM (CBVM) algorithm, a meta-heuristic optimization approach inspired by the Hindu Trimurti-Lord Brahma, Vishnu, and Mahesh. Reflecting their divine roles, the algorithm consists of three phases: population generation (Brahma), position updating to preserve diversity (Vishnu), and elimination of inferior solutions (Mahesh). To enhance the balance between exploration and exploitation, CBVM incorporates chaotic maps, improving search efficiency, population diversity, and convergence speed while reducing the risk of premature convergence. The performance of CBVM is evaluated on the CEC2005 and CEC2019 benchmark suites and statistically validated using t-test, Friedman test, and Wilcoxon rank-sum test. Experimental results demonstrate that CBVM consistently outperforms several existing algorithms by effectively avoiding local optima and achieving superior global convergence. Furthermore, its successful application to real-world engineering design problems highlights its robustness, adaptability, and effectiveness in solving both constrained and unconstrained optimization problems.

title: AI Cracks Jokes: Building Consumer–Brand Closeness Through Machine‐Generated Humor
abstract: ABSTRACT Integrating AI led social cues into service encounters has become a key strategy for humanizing technology. Grounded in Social Penetration Theory, this research examines how AI‐generated humor styles (affiliative vs. self‐defeating) influence consumer brand identification and proposes consumer personality as a key moderator. To ensure methodological rigor, we employ a multi‐study experimental design across four independent studies, each using scenario‐based experiments with controlled manipulations and separate participant samples. Results show that AI humor operates as socio‐emotional disclosure that strengthens brand connections. Both humor styles significantly enhance brand identification relative to neutral interactions, through the parallel mediating roles of psychological closeness and customer trust. Drawing on Benign Violation Theory to clarify boundary conditions, the findings reveal a moderating effect of consumer personality. Extraverts respond positively to both humor types due to higher stimulation tolerance, whereas introverts show a clear preference for affiliative humor and view self‐defeating humor as risky or inappropriate. These results reconcile inconsistencies in human AI interaction research and offer practical insights for leveraging person AI fit to build authentic digital relationships.

title: Exploring Harmony in Mission Engineering via Explainable Complex Game Design
abstract: Abstract In this paper, we explore bringing harmony between human decision making and machine learning in the mission engineering domain by using explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) and uncertainty quantification (UQ). This study focuses on game design, which is used as an abstraction of mission engineering. We implement a closed‐loop three‐layer framework for transparent optimization in design scenarios with large design spaces. This study uses a popular and complex real‐time strategy game, StarCraft II (SC2), to build a complex game design problem. Many full‐length SC2 games on a 64X64 map, between identical SC2 bot players with varying units specified via a design of experiments (DOE), are played to generate gameplay data comprising win and loss information along with spatial and tabular gameplay data. This data is then used to train a convolutional neural network (CNN) model to predict the winner using initial and transient game settings. To implement UQ, we used Monte Carlo Dropout Networks (MCDNs). We achieved a validation accuracy of 91.5% in all game frames in the holdout set for this model. The Shapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) toolbox is used to explain the model predictions and works as an XAI tool. The SHAP provides information on game balance by identifying the most important features on the input game design space in each game frame. We demonstrate our framework using an example game‐play in which SHAP uncovers the most significant feature that decides the win or loss for a given player. The proposed framework can be generalized, is extensible to other design problems, and can be used to solve real mission engineering problems.

title: $\text{Log}_\text{b}$Quant: Quantizing Language Models in Logarithmic Space
abstract: Quantization has become an invaluable tool to reduce memory requirements and inference speed of modern language models, in particular to make them available for consumer setups and edge devices. While previous work has primarily focused on uniform quantization codebooks, such approaches are prone to suboptimal representations due to low-frequency high-magnitude weights. We introduce Log$_\text{b}$Quant, a novel logarithmic quantization approach with adjustable bases, to adapt to common parameter distributions. We show that our method exhibits superior performance at 4-bit precision on several performance benchmarks compared to asymmetric linear quantization at tensor-wise granularity, while achieving moderate speedup and high memory savings, making it suitable for private use on consumer-grade GPUs.

title: DroneIQA-VLE: Multi-Task Drone Image Quality Assessment via Vision-Language Ensemble
abstract: We present DroneIQA-VLE, our solution to the ICME 2026 Drone-IQA Grand Challenge on Target-aware Image Quality Assessment for Low-altitude UAV Images. The framework jointly predicts global, target, and background quality scores by ensembling two complementary pipelines: (1) SigLIP2 vision encoders with multi-task regression heads, and (2) a LoRA-adapted Qwen3.5-9B multimodal large language model for quality score regression. The final global quality prediction is obtained by arithmetically averaging the outputs of both pipelines. Our method achieves 2nd place in the challenge, demonstrating its effectiveness. The code is available at https://github.com/sunwei925/DroneIQA-VLE.

title: Natural language to SPARQL translation with compact encoder-decoder models: an empirical study on Wikidata and DBpedia
abstract: Esta tesis analiza la eficacia de modelos compactos encoder–decoder basados en Transformers para esta tarea. En lugar de asumir que los modelos de gran tamaño son siempre necesarios, se investiga hasta qué punto arquitecturas más pequeñas pueden alcanzar un buen rendimiento mediante fine-tuning y mejoras en la representación de la entrada. Se evalúan cuatro modelos bajo condiciones experimentales idénticas en dos grafos de conocimiento ampliamente utilizados. Los resultados experimentales muestran que los modelos compactos pueden generar consultas SPARQL de alta calidad tras un ajuste supervisado. La incorporación explícita de anotaciones de entidades en la entrada aporta una mejora adicional en los modelos más robustos (CodeT5-small y mT5-small), pero resulta perjudicial para T5- small y BART-base, lo que indica que su beneficio depende de la arquitectura y no es universal. Al mismo tiempo, el análisis revela patrones de error característicos que no quedan reflejados completamente por métricas léxicas tradicionales, incluyendo alucinaciones de URIs y errores en la predicción de identificadores. Esto pone de manifiesto la necesidad de complementar las métricas automáticas con evaluaciones basadas en ejecución y análisis cualitativos. En conjunto, los resultados indican que los modelos encoder–decoder eficientes siguen siendo una alternativa práctica y relevante para la traducción de lenguaje natural a SPARQL. Más allá de los modelos concretos evaluados, este trabajo destaca la importancia de la representación de la entrada, el manejo de identificadores y la metodología de evaluación en la investigación sobre semantic parsing en grafos de conocimiento. --ABSTRACT-- Knowledge graphs such as DBpedia and Wikidata store large amounts of structured information, yet accessing this knowledge typically requires SPARQL, a query language that is difficult for non-expert users. Automatically translating natural language questions into SPARQL queries is therefore a key step toward more accessible knowledge graph interfaces. This thesis investigates the effectiveness of compact Transformer-based encoder– decoder models for this task. Instead of assuming that large-scale language models are always required, it explores how smaller architectures can achieve strong performance through fine-tuning and improved input representations. Four pre-trained models are evaluated under identical experimental conditions on two widely used knowledge graphs. The experimental results show that compact models can generate high-quality SPARQL queries after supervised fine-tuning. Explicitly including entity annotations in the input provides a further gain for the strongest models (CodeT5-small and mT5-small), but proves detrimental for T5-small and BART-base, indicating that its benefit is architecture-dependent rather than universal. Meanwhile, the analysis reveals characteristic error patterns that are not fully captured by traditional lexical metrics, including URI hallucinations and identifier prediction errors. This highlights the importance of complementing automatic evaluation with execution-based and qualitative analysis. Overall, the findings indicate that efficient encoder–decoder models remain a practical and competitive approach for natural language to SPARQL translation. Beyond the specific models evaluated, this work emphasizes the importance of input representation, identifier handling, and evaluation methodology in semantic parsing over knowledge graphs.

title: Hybrid Deep Learning with Explainable AI for Breast Cancer Prediction Using the WBCD Dataset
abstract: Breast cancer remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality among women worldwide, creating demand for diagnostic models that are both accurate and interpretable. While machine learning and deep learning methods have achieved strong results on benchmark datasets, such as the Wisconsin Breast Cancer Diagnostic (WBCD) dataset, limitations including class imbalance, overfitting, and lack of interpretability hinder their clinical use. This study proposes a hybrid deep learning framework that integrates Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) with Gated Recurrent Units (GRU), supported by class weighting and stratified sampling to address class imbalance, and SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) to enhance model transparency. Preprocessing involved KNN imputation for missing values, label encoding, and Min-Max normalization. The model was evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and AUC-ROC. On the WBCD dataset, the CNN–GRU achieved 95.61% accuracy, 100.0% precision, 88.10% recall, 93.67% F1-score, and 0.9944 AUC-ROC. The absence of false positives underscores the model’s conservative boundary, though five false negatives highlight sensitivity trade-offs. SHAP-based global and local explanations identified concave points, perimeter, and radius as the most influential features, consistent with clinical knowledge and providing insight into both correct and incorrect classifications. Unlike prior studies that reported higher accuracies but offered limited interpretability, the proposed framework strikes a balance between predictive strength and clinical trustworthiness. These findings position CNN–GRU with explainable AI as a promising tool for decision support in breast cancer diagnosis and point to future directions in multimodal integration, federated learning, and prospective clinical validation.

title: The Executive AI Leverage Report (Preview Edition)
abstract: The Executive AI Leverage Report (Preview Edition) examines how AI leverage is experienced across the executive suite as a whole, rather than within a single function. It introduces the Executive AI Leverage Ladder, a three-stage framework describing how executives get leverage from AI: productivity (AI as a thought partner), capability (AI as a co-worker completing whole units of work), and context (AI that understands the business well enough to ask its own questions). Findings combine quantitative survey data from finance, security, marketing, and founder audiences with qualitative practices drawn from Open Future Forum peer-learning sessions. Quantitative findings come from an instrument embedded in applications to seven Open Future Forum events in 2026, with 421 applicants answering at least one instrument question. This is a preview edition; full methodology notes accompany the canonical report. Canonical source: https://openfutureforum.com/research/executive-ai-leverage-report

title: **Cross-lingual Transfer Performance with Multilingual Intermediate Tasks in 1B--10B Parameter Models**
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. We see large improvements from intermediate training on the BUCC and Tatoeba sentence retrieval tas Research goal: What is the impact of combining multiple non-English intermediate tasks from diverse languages on zero-shot cross-lingual transfer performance in the XTREME benchmark for models between 1B and 10B parameters, compared to using only English intermediate tasks? Autonomous synthesis report generated by Assignee Research. Tribunal consensus score: 9.3/10.

title: ReplyIQ: A Prompt-Orchestrated LLM Architecture for Unified Inbox Automation, Sentiment-Aware Routing, and Lead Scoring
abstract: This paper presents ReplyIQ, a Next.js/Supabase customer-engagement platform that uses a single hosted large language model (Gemini 1.5 Flash) behind twelve independent prompt-templated API routes to provide reply drafting, sentiment classification, lead detection and scoring, promise extraction, appointment detection, and follow-up generation over a simulated unified inbox spanning WhatsApp, Instagram, and websitechat channels. The system’s relational schema and prompt orchestration pattern are documented in detail, along with – critically – the fact that channel ingestion is currently simulatedby a template-driven message generator rather than connected to live messaging APIs, a distinction the public-facing description of the system does not make explicit. In place of fabricated production metrics, a small, fully disclosed component-level evaluation is reported, executed directly against the deployed code: a robustness test of the regex-based Markdown-code-fencestripping routine that sits between every LLM call and the application’s JSON parsing layer, including a controlled ablationisolating the stripping step’s contribution, and a structural comparison with a more defensive JSON-repair routine takenfrom an unrelated codebase by the same author. The engineering and architectural trade-offs of using prompt engineering over a single foundation model as the entire “AI layer” of a multi-feature SaaS product are discussed, concrete robustness and security limitations are identified, and the system is positioned within the recent literature on LLM-based sentiment analysis and lead scoring for customer engagement.

title: BU251 Explainability and Verifiability Toolchain under B_U BU251|B_U 体系下的可解释性与可证性工具链 Formal Step Checker, Evidence Chain, Deployment Gate, Runtime Assurance, Residual Audit, and Settlement-Gated Verification 形式步骤检查器、证据链、部署门禁、运行时保证、残差审计与结算门控型验证
abstract: BU251 establishes Explainability and Verifiability Toolchain under B_U as a deployment-facing framework for converting AI explanations, formal proofs, benchmark results, logs, telemetry, provenance records, human review, and regulatory evidence into a unified standing audit chain. Its central thesis is that explainability is not the production of persuasive explanatory text, and verifiability is not the possession of a formal proof, benchmark score, or compliance document. Under B_U, both must enter a reality-settlement interface where object boundaries, semantic fidelity, invariant kernels, evidence chains, runtime behavior, residual ledgers, responsibility chains, and feedback gates remain auditable. The file connects the formal-handshake axis of BU109–BU130 with the deployment and reality-settlement engineering axis of BU242–BU250. It treats proof admissibility, benchmark validity, model equivalence, statistical sufficiency, distributed consistency, semantic fidelity, invariant kernel preservation, transport mapping, residual reaggregation, and standing transfer as components of a single verification stack. A system does not obtain standing because it can explain an answer, pass a test, or produce a proof. It obtains standing only when the explanation points to the correct object, the proof targets the declared boundary, the evidence chain is traceable, the semantic object remains stable across transformations, runtime feedback is recorded, residuals are ranked and cleared, responsibility is assigned, and deployment gates can admit, hold, repair, rollback, retire, or re-admit the system. BU251 introduces an end-to-end architecture composed of an object registry, formal step checker, evidence-chain ledger, semantic fidelity gate, runtime assurance layer, residual audit engine, and deployment decision engine. The formal step checker validates proof steps, theorem targets, type witnesses, benchmark-target alignment, and specification-to-implementation relations. The evidence-chain ledger binds source records, logs, tests, proofs, credentials, timestamps, signatures, provenance graphs, telemetry, and decision traces. The semantic fidelity gate ensures that explanations, memory states, model outputs, tool calls, APIs, and human-facing documentation refer to the same object rather than drifting across contexts. The file also defines five verification workflows: formal proof verification, model and benchmark validation, runtime and deployment assurance, cross-domain cyber-physical verification, and regulatory or responsibility audit. These workflows are not interchangeable. Formal proof validates derivation under declared assumptions; benchmark validation checks behavior under a protocol; runtime assurance determines whether the deployed system remains within boundary; cross-domain verification checks whether state and meaning survive transport; regulatory audit checks whether responsibility, documentation, and evidence can support institutional review. BU251 further emphasizes adversarial resilience and re-admission. Explanations can be fabricated, benchmarks can be gamed, logs can be suppressed, memories can be poisoned, telemetry can be spoofed, and models can be silently substituted. Therefore, high-risk deployment requires signed evidence, provenance, runtime monitoring, incident reconstruction, residual accounting, human oversight, and re-admission protocols after repair. The final claim is direct: explainability is an evidence chain, not explanatory prose; verifiability is a deployment gate, not proof theater. A system becomes explainable and verifiable under B_U only when object, proof, evidence, semantics, runtime, residuals, responsibility, feedback, and gate decisions jointly settle into retained standing.

title: Weakly Supervised Synthetic Data Generation via Data Programming and SMOTE
abstract: Class imbalance and the scarcity of high-quality labeled data represent two major bottlenecks that severely limit the performance of machine learning models in real-world applications. Traditional Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) alleviates class imbalance by interpolating between minority instances, but it relies heavily on the availability of accurate, manually annotated labels. To address this limitation, this paper proposes DP-SMOTE, a novel synthetic data generation framework that integrates data programming with the SMOTE algorithm under a weak supervision paradigm. Instead of relying on gold-standard labels, the proposed method leverages a system of heuristic labeling functions designed by domain experts. A generative model is then utilized to estimate the accuracies and correlations of these functions, assigning probabilistic labels to unlabeled data without ground truth. These probabilistic labels are subsequently incorporated into a modified SMOTE mechanism, which employs probability-weighted sampling and data-driven interpolation boundaries to generate high-quality synthetic minority samples while suppressing the generation of boundary noise. The proposed framework effectively tackles both class imbalance and label scarcity simultaneously, offering a robust data augmentation solution for weakly supervised scenarios.

title: An Oversampling Algorithm for Imbalanced Data Classification Based on Subspace Stitching SMOTE
abstract: Class imbalance is a pervasive and challenging issue in data mining and machine learning. Traditional synthetic minority over-sampling techniques (SMOTE) often suffer from the "curse of dimensionality" when dealing with high-dimensional data, where distance metrics lose their distinctiveness, leading to the generation of noisy or suboptimal samples. To address this limitation, this paper proposes a novel over-sampling approach termed Subspace Stitching SMOTE (SS-SMOTE). The core idea of SS-SMOTE is to decompose the high-dimensional feature space into multiple mutually disjoint, low-dimensional subspaces. Local nearest neighbor selection and linear interpolation are then independently executed within each low-dimensional subspace to generate localized sample fragments. Finally, a randomized cross-stitching mechanism is employed to concatenate these low-dimensional fragments from different synthesized sources into complete, high-dimensional minority class samples. This subspace-based approach effectively preserves local feature correlations and circumvents global distance distortion. By breaking the rigid bonds of global features, the proposed cross-stitching mechanism substantially enhances the diversity and quality of the synthetic samples, thereby expanding the decision boundaries effectively. The proposed algorithm provides a robust and scalable solution for handling high-dimensional imbalanced data classification tasks without compromising local manifold structures.

title: Wind–Solar Resource Assessment and Optimal Siting in Desert–Gobi–Wilderness Regions: A Case Study of the Badain Jaran and Kumtag Deserts
abstract: With the advancement of China’s “dual carbon” targets, Desert–Gobi–Wilderness (DGW) regions have become strategic areas for large-scale renewable energy deployment. However, the intermittency and variability of wind and solar resources pose challenges to power system stability, necessitating systematic evaluation of their characteristics and complementarity. This study uses ERA5 reanalysis data (2013–2023) to assess wind and solar resources in the Badain Jaran and Kumtag Deserts. A multi-dimensional framework is developed, incorporating availability, intermittency, variability, and complementarity, and a GIS-based multi-criteria decision-making method is applied for site selection. Results show that the Badain Jaran Desert is characterised by strong wind resources (average wind power density: 235.16 W/m2) and is suitable for wind-dominated development, whereas the Kumtag Desert exhibits superior solar resources (221.08 W/m2), favouring photovoltaic deployment. Significant wind–solar complementarity is identified, particularly in the central-western Badain Jaran and northeastern Kumtag regions. Three high-suitability sites were identified, including two in the Badain Jaran Desert and one in the Kumtag Desert, all characterised by favourable topographic conditions and high engineering feasibility. This study provides a scientific basis and a methodological framework for the planning of wind–solar hybrid systems and coordinated ecological development in DGW regions.
